title-group.article-title: Real-world outcomes with trastuzumab deruxtecan in HER2-low metastatic breast cancer.

abstract.p: Background: trastuzumab deruxtecan is used for patients with HER2-low metastatic breast cancer, but real-world evidence regarding outcomes after prior therapy remains limited. We evaluated treatment effectiveness and safety in routine clinical practice. Methods: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 184 adults treated with trastuzumab deruxtecan at 4 oncology centers between 2021 and 2025. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival. Secondary endpoints included overall survival, treatment discontinuation, dose modification, and documented adverse events. Results: Median follow-up was 18.2 months. Median progression-free survival was 7.6 months and median overall survival was 19.4 months. Objective response was observed in 48% of evaluable patients. Dose modification occurred in 27% and treatment discontinuation because of toxicity occurred in 9%. Conclusions: In this real-world cohort, trastuzumab deruxtecan demonstrated clinically meaningful activity with a manageable safety profile in patients with HER2-low metastatic breast cancer. Prospective studies are needed to confirm these findings. Research Sponsor: None.
